title: Evidence supply-chain mapping and audit FAQ
content:
Purpose:
This note defines an evidence supply-chain view for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls that intersect with RBAC v2, the audit-log schema, SIEM exports, and our evidence automation pipeline. It is intended as a reviewer-facing brief for auditors and as a working remediation tracker for SRE / Platform teams.

Scope:
- Controls: SOC 2 CC6 (Access Controls), CC7 (Change Management), CC3 (System Operations), and ISO 27001 Annex A.9 (Access control), A.12 (Operations), A.16 (Incident management).
- Systems: Identity Provider (IdP), RBAC v2 service (authz-api), serving-runtime audit logger, SIEM export pipeline (kinesis -> splunk/elastic), evidence-store (S3 + Glacier lifecycle).
- Evidence types: role assignments, policy change history, token issuance logs, admin console audit trails, SIEM ingestion receipts, signed export manifests.

Quick traceability examples (abbreviated):
- Control: Access provisioning (SOC2 CC6.1 / ISO A.9.2) -> Evidence: idp-provisioning-log, rbac-v2-assignment-audit, onboarding Jira ticket metadata -> Location: s3://evidence/access-provisioning/<date>/manifest.json -> Notes: rbac-v2 captures pre/post policy diffs starting 2024-11-01.
- Control: Admin actions (ISO A.9.4) -> Evidence: admin-console-audit, session-token-events -> Location: SIEM index admin_actions-* -> Notes: admin-console emits structured JSON with actor_id, operation, target_resource, outcome, tx_id.
- Control: Configuration changes (SOC2 CC7) -> Evidence: git PRs, config-change webhook events, runtime reload events -> Location: github PR link + audit-log entry tx_id -> Notes: need stronger linking between PR ids and runtime reload txs (gap #3).

Observed gaps (high level):
1) Lacking canonical tx_id linking across GitHub PRs -> config-change webhook -> runtime reload audit event. Impact: harder to produce end-to-end change evidence for CC7. (Owner: platform-eng)
2) RBAC v2 role inheritance edge cases are not captured in exported SIEM schema (no "effective_roles" field). Impact: auditor cannot always prove effective permission set at time X. (Owner: authz-api)
3) SIEM export retention mismatch: SIEM index retained 90 days; SOC2 evidence requests sometimes require 1 year. We currently rely on S3 export jobs but the automation is not fully validated. (Owner: observability)
4) Evidence manifests are unsigned for automated exports. Need an HMAC or signature to demonstrate export integrity. (Owner: security-engineering)

Planned remediations and priorities (short roadmap):
- Q1 2025: Add canonical tx_id propagation pipeline. Steps: GitHub webhook -> CI emits tx_id -> config-change webhook includes tx_id -> runtime audit-log includes tx_id. Target: end-to-end traceability for config changes. (JIRA JIRA-2126)
- Q1 2025: Extend audit-log schema to include effective_roles and role_delta for RBAC v2 evaluation events. Backfill tooling for common queries.
- Q2 2025: Implement signed export manifests (HMAC with KMS key) and add verification step in evidence ingestion lambda.
- Q2 2025: Adjust SIEM export retention and add automated rehydration proofs (daily checksum + s3 lifecycle proof).

SIEM export notes (current implementation and shortfalls):
- Pipeline: audit-logger -> kinesis -> firehose -> s3 (parquet) -> periodic ingestion to Splunk/Elastic.
- Export schema: timestamp, actor_id, event_type, resource, outcome, metadata (json blob).
- Shortfalls: metadata blob is free-form; lacks structured fields for policy_version, tx_id, and effective_roles. Splunk parsers exist but are fragile.
- Quick mitigation: add structured meta fields (policy_version, tx_id) to the top-level schema before the next major rollout.

RBAC v2 considerations (auditor focus):
- Snapshotability: auditors will request proof of role state at point-in-time. We must ensure rbac-v2 writes immutable snapshots for events that alter role bindings.
- Delegation: audit how delegated role owners are recorded (actor_id and delegation_proof).
- Automated provisioning: tie IdP provisioning events to RBAC bindings using the canonical tx_id.

Evidence automation (practical checklist):
- Ensure export manifests include: export_id, start_ts, end_ts, item_count, checksum, signer_kid.
- Verify ingestion logs: ingestion_success boolean + ingestion_tx_id in evidence-store.
- For manual evidence pulls: maintain an audit ticket (Jira) and attach the signed manifest URL.

Auditor Q&A prep (sample Qs and prepared answers):
Q: How do you prove a user did or did not have admin rights on 2024-12-15?
A: Provide rbac-v2 snapshot for 2024-12-15 (stored in s3://evidence/rbac-snapshots/2024-12-15.json), cross-reference with idp group membership export (idp-exports/2024-12-15.json) and admin-console-audit entries between 2024-12-15T00:00 and 2024-12-16T00:00. The snapshots include policy_version and binding_tx_id. (Action: run snapshot generator if missing - JIRA JIRA-2334)

Q: Can you show proof that export files were not tampered with after generation?
A: Exports will be accompanied by an HMAC signature (s3 manifest signer_kid) and a checksum recorded in the evidence-store. The ingestion lambda verifies the signature and logs verification events to the audit index.

Q: How are privileged role changes approved?
A: Privileged changes must follow the privileged-access flow: GitHub PR with "privileged-access" label, 2 approvers from the security team, CI gated job that emits tx_id and creates a Jira approval record. The runtime rejects un-signed config reloads for privileged paths.

Open questions / risks to resolve before audit:
- Q1: Can we backfill effective_roles for historical events? If not, can we produce combined evidence from snapshots + SIEM queries to approximate? (Owner: authz-api)
- Q2: SLA for evidence retrieval for requests older than SIEM retention window (owner: observability + security).
- Q3: Operational cost for extended SIEM retention vs. on-demand rehydration. Need finance estimate.

Action items (next 30 days):
- Platform-eng: prototype tx_id event propagation (POC due 2025-01-24) -> contact: Liam Carter.
- Authz-api: PR to add effective_roles field and schema migration plan (PR-1043).
- Observability: run proof-of-concept signed-manifest ingestion and publish runbook (owner: Asha Patel).

Useful links and artifacts:
- Control mapping matrix (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Control+Mapping+Matrix
- RBAC v2 design notes: github.com/redwood-inference/authz/design/rbac-v2.md
- SIEM export spec: s3://redwood-evidence-bucket/specs/siem-export-spec-2024-11.md

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working playbook. Expect a mix of TODOs and concrete deliverables. Use linked JIRA/GitHub artifacts when preparing auditor bundles. If you are the auditor liaison, annotate which evidence pieces you need in the ticket and mark the priority.

-- Maya
